svg.title: The stage graph of run_pipeline.py
svg.desc: Three bands. The top band, drawn with dashed borders and a marked spine, is what an agent owes before the runner can start. The middle band is the sixteen deterministic stages the runner executes in order, from prompts through to manifest, wrapping left to right across four rows of four. Four stages are gates. Two of them, structures and translations, stop the run, because everything downstream consumes what they produce. The other two, visual and verify, are drawn with dashed borders: they produce terminal artifacts nothing else reads, so each records its failure and sets the exit code while letting the rest of the run finish. A dotted line links stage 7 to stage 12, which run the same script twice. A panel down the right-hand side is the deliverable tree every stage writes into.
svg.text: One patent in, a complete deliverable out

LEGEND · every distinction below is carried by a shape or a word as well as by a colour, so the diagram survives greyscale
solid thin border · deterministic stage, run by run_pipeline.py
thick SOLID border, octagon marked GATE · everything downstream needs it, so it stops the run
thick DASHED border · gate on a terminal artifact: records the failure, sets the exit code, does not stop the run
dashed border, marked spine · NOT run by the script; an agent or a human produces it
solid arrow · the next stage consumes what this one wrote
dotted arrow · the same script, run a second time
Exit: 1 stage failed, 2 gate, 3 passes not run, 4 wrong patent, 5 bad biblio.
A stage that failed last time always runs again: the manifest remembers.
